name: Stop missing calls: Reception by ElevenAgents
object: Reception, an AI phone receptionist agent built on ElevenAgents that answers calls and books appointments automatically
audience: Small and service businesses (tradespeople, clinics, salons) who lose jobs when no one is free to pick up the phone
message: This video tells small-business owners that every unanswered call is a lost job or client, and Reception answers instantly, in a natural-sounding voice, so nothing falls through.

moments.what: Fast-cut flat icon animation: a phone ringing, a thumbs-down, icons of a call coming in.
moments.copy: Someone's calling to make an appointment.

moments.what: More icons stack up over ringing desk phones and a buzzing mobile — a job to book, a meeting to schedule — until the line lands on an empty office.
moments.copy: To book a job. To schedule a meeting. But nobody's around to pick up.

moments.what: Cut to a real call in progress: a calm, natural AI voice answers and starts booking a slot for the caller.
moments.copy: "Hi there, how can I help you today?" / "I'm looking to book an appointment for next week."

moments.what: Voiceover pitches the product by name while the booking call keeps running underneath it.
moments.copy: Stop missing calls and losing clients with the most natural-sounding AI receptionist — Reception, by ElevenAgents.

cta: A direct spoken CTA names the product outright — "stop missing calls and losing clients ... with Reception, by ElevenAgents" — delivered as voiceover over the still-running demo call, so the pitch and the proof land in the same beat instead of a separate end card.
why: It opens on the viewer's own pain (a call nobody answers) before it shows a single feature, so by the time the AI voice picks up, the viewer already wants that outcome. Keeping the demo call audible under the CTA line is what sells it — the voice doing the selling is the exact voice doing the selling job described.
